clue.text: Wander about listlessly after depressing astronomical event

indicators.note: after places the drifting word behind the gloomy one

parts.note: something depressing is blue, gloomy
to moon about is to drift aimlessly

explanation.surface: Someone mopes around aimlessly after witnessing some gloomy happening in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A second full moon within one calendar month is a rare sky event, hence the idiom for rarity.

clue.text: Take responsibility for catching extremely valuable animal

indicators.note: catching means the bearing word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to bear something is to shoulder it

indicators.note: extremely takes the outside letters of valuable

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of capturing a highly prized creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The beaver is a large dam-building rodent, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Shot over earlier disturbance

indicators.note: earlier puts the finished word ahead of the go

parts.note: up means over, finished, as in time's up
a shot is a go, a turn

explanation.surface: A gunshot ringing out above an earlier commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot over' reads as a phrase, but 'over' goes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn can mean an upheaval, a sudden overturning or commotion, as Chambers records.

clue.text: Norm made off before first of appointment reminders

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of that letter
off means the letters have gone bad, out of shape
first of takes the opening letter of appointment

explanation.surface: Norm left before the first appointment reminders arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda, plural of memorandum, are notes written to jog the memory.

clue.text: Wonderful without folds or flounces

indicators.note: flounces, as a verb, means flings about wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Praise for a dress that is marvellous without pleats or frills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounces' looks like dressmaking, ruffles on a skirt, but works as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extraordinarily good, as though from another planet, so marvellous.

clue.text: Board's academic qualification obtained by queen before king

indicators.note: before puts the queen-and-degree group ahead of the king's letter
obtained by means the queen's letters hold the degree within them

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, abbreviates queen
MBA is the Master of Business Administration degree
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A board's degree certificate is acquired by a queen ahead of a king, like a royal pecking order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board's' is 'Board is': the definition is the verb, to board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a ship or plane is to get on it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Recurrent theme of uncertainty associated with Mailer's earliest books

indicators.note: earliest takes the first letter of the novelist's name

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
if expresses doubt, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Discussing Norman Mailer's early novels, which keep returning to doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a repeated idea or pattern running through a work of art.

clue.text: In spite of retaining you it's mentioned seconds after each game

indicators.note: after places the seconds letter at the end

parts.note: all can mean each, as in a score of two all

indicators.note: retaining means the despite word holds that letter within it

parts.note: for can mean despite, as in for all his efforts

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so we take the letter that sounds like the word you

parts.note: the word you is said aloud as a letter

explanation.surface: A grumble that despite you being kept on, seconds follow every match.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL here is the 'all' of drawn scores, two all.
explanation.definitionFit: All fours is an old card game, the name also of crawling on hands and knees.

clue.text: Fuel rumours of subterfuge initially swallowed by enthusiastic European

indicators.note: swallowed by means those letters go inside the eager word

parts.note: keen means eager, enthusiastic

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of rumours, of and subterfuge

explanation.surface: Gossip of underhand dealings is lapped up by an eager continental, fuelling the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin oil, burnt as fuel in lamps, heaters and jet engines.

clue.text: Official threat shaped by a firmly held belief

indicators.note: shaped means the letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A threat from the authorities, formed by a deep conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a tenet held with unquestioning conviction, a creed's core belief.

clue.text: Try crack

definitions.meaning: a try is an effort or go at something
to have a crack at something is to have a go

explanation.surface: Two words, both meaning an effort or a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a try and a crack are an effort, an endeavour or shot at doing something.

clue.text: Repelled at first by toy snake

indicators.note: by here means next to, so the letter sits beside the toy

parts.note: a rattle is a baby's noisy toy

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of Repelled

explanation.surface: Someone was initially put off by a toy snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is an informal American name for the rattlesnake, a venomous viper.

clue.text: Trapped inside after Rory's blunder

indicators.note: trapped inside says the letters lie captured within the words after Rory's

explanation.surface: Someone stuck indoors, following Rory, makes a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'after' into 'Rory's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is a mistake, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Goes crazy over failure caused by reversals of policy in Washington

indicators.note: over means the crazy word goes over, enclosing, the failure word

parts.note: to flip is to lose one's temper or go mad
a flop is a failure

explanation.surface: Someone goes mad about a failure caused by US policy U-turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip-flop is US political slang for a sudden reversal of a stated position.

clue.text: Eventually becoming fashionable at that time to admit covering a great distance before game

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: to admit means the time word lets the distance and game letters inside it

parts.note: then means at that time

indicators.note: before puts the distance word ahead of the game

parts.note: long describes something stretching a great distance
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Something becomes trendy once a long trek is followed by a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means after a long period, ultimately, so it matches eventually.

clue.text: Open-air buffet in the centre of Henley is without equal

indicators.note: to buffet is to knock about, so these letters are battered into a new order
in the centre of takes the middle two letters of Henley

explanation.surface: An outdoor buffet at Henley Regatta is said to be unrivalled.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley is a Thames town famed for its rowing regatta. 'buffet' looks like a meal but is the verb; it mixes OPENAIR with NL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil, from French for having no equal, describes something unrivalled or matchless.

clue.text: Proust edges away after strikebreaker becomes unpleasant

indicators.note: after puts the trimmed name behind the strikebreaker

parts.note: scab is a derogatory term for a worker who crosses a picket line

indicators.note: edges away means the outside letters of the writer's name are removed

explanation.surface: Proust slinks off after a strike-breaker turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabrous means rough or indecent, hence distasteful and offensive.

clue.text: Made a copy of papers including note to gallery

indicators.note: including means the papers letters contain the others

parts.note: ID means identity papers
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Documents with a note to an art gallery were forged.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy, mimic or reproduce, so imitated means copied.

clue.text: Bed broken by politician finding passion out east for instance

indicators.note: out means the letters of passion are disturbed, put out of order

explanation.surface: A bed wrecked by a politician whose passion has gone, east of somewhere perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns passion into ASSPOIN. 'east' looks like a wordplay letter E to place, but 'east for instance' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the cardinal directions marked on a compass, an example of the category.

clue.text: Language of denial gripping island in recession

indicators.note: gripping means the denial holds the other letters

parts.note: no is a denial

parts.note: Java is an island of Indonesia

clue.text: Odd characters from Leek involved in cult by choice

indicators.note: odd characters means the first and third letters of Leek

explanation.walkthrough: Leek is a Staffordshire market town.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, choice and select both mean of the finest quality, hand-picked.

clue.text: Gambler leaving richer

parts.note: a better is one who bets
to be off is to be leaving

explanation.surface: A gambler walks away wealthier.
explanation.definitionFit: Being better off means being in better financial circumstances, wealthier.

clue.text: Priest turning against poet

indicators.note: turning means the against word is written backwards

parts.note: to can mean against, as in shoulder to shoulder

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns against a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was a celebrated modernist poet, author of The Waste Land.

clue.text: Saw letters from Mossad agents

indicators.note: letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, as in 'an old saw'.

clue.text: Being tested by Repton's head in translation of Old Latin

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the rearranged letters
translation of means the letters are turned into another form, rearranged
head takes the first letter of the school's name

explanation.surface: A Repton headmaster's skill is examined by translating Old Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: Repton is an English public school. 'translation of' makes ONTIAL from O plus LATIN, and R goes in.

clue.text: Repeat it time after time before start of Eid

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of Eid

explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, a direct synonym of repeat.

clue.text: Dignified in court after witness falls short

parts.note: to witness is to see
to court is to date, woo

explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal but is the verb, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm, composed and unhurried, which is a dignified bearing.

clue.text: Revealed after letter gets students to calm down

indicators.note: after puts the revealed word behind the letter and students

L is a learner, so LL is two students
something revealed is out

explanation.surface: Once a letter brings the students' secrets into the open, everyone should relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Chill out is slang for relax, unwind and stop being agitated.
